{{nihongo|'''Meta Shrine'''|賣太神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

'''Meta Shrine''' (めたじんじゃ, '''Urita Shrine''') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located at the edge of the Hieda {{ill|Moated settlements|ja|環濠集落|qid=Q60995739}} in {{ill|Yamatokōriyama|Q118213|qid=Q118213}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Nara|af|Nara-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Nara|ar|نارا (محافظة)|az|Nara prefekturası|azb|نارا اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Nara|bat_smg|Naras prefektūra|be|Нара (прэфектура)|bg|Нара (префектура)|bn|নারা প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Nara|cdo|Nara-gâing|ce|Нара (префектура)|ceb|Nara-ken|ckb|پارێزگای نارا|cs|Prefektura Nara|cy|Nara (talaith)|da|Nara-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Nara|eo|Gubernio Nara|es|Prefectura de Nara|et|Nara prefektuur|eu|Nara (prefektura)|fa|استان نارا|fi|Naran prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Nara|frr|Nara (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Nara|gl|Prefectura de Nara|gor|Prefektur Nara|hak|Nara-yen|he|נארה (מחוז)|hr|Nara (prefektura)|hu|Nara prefektúra|hy|Նարա (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Nara|ilo|Prepektura ti Nara|it|Prefettura di Nara|ja|奈良県|jv|Préfèktur Nara|ka|ნარის პრეფექტურა|kk|Нара (префектура)|km|ណារ៉ា(ខេត្ត)|ko|나라현|la|Naraënsis|lt|Naros prefektūra|lv|Naras prefektūra|mk|Нара (префектура)|mni|ꯅꯥꯔꯥ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|नारा प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Nara|my|နာရခရိုင်|nl|Nara (prefectuur)|no|Nara (prefektur)|os|Нарæ (префектурæ)|pam|Prepektura ning Nara|pl|Prefektura Nara|pnb|ضلع نارا|pt|Nara (prefeitura)|ro|Prefectura Nara|ru|Нара (префектура)|sco|Nara Prefectur|sd|نارا پريفيڪچر|se|Nara prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Nara|si|නාරා ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Nara Prefecture|sk|Nara (prefektúra)|sl|Prefektura Nara|sr|Префектура Нара|su|Nara Prefecture|sv|Nara prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Nara|ta|நாரா மாநிலம்|tg|Префектураи Нара|th|จังหวัดนาระ|tl|Prepektura ng Nara|tok|ma Nala|tr|Nara (prefektörlük)|tt|Нара (префектура)|uk|Префектура Нара|ur|نارا پریفیکچر|vi|Nara (tỉnh)|war|Nara (prefektura)|wuu|奈良县|zh|奈良县|zh_classical|奈良縣|zh_min_nan|Nara-koān|zh_yue|奈良縣|qid=Q131287}}. It is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system#miscellaneous shrines}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
It enshrines {{ill|Hieda no Are|Q164522|qid=Q164522}}, who was involved in the compilation of the {{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}, as the principal deity (main enshrined deity), with {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|ar|أمه نو أوزومه|as|আমে-ন′-উজুমে|bcl|Ama-no-Uzume|ca|Ama-no-Uzume|cs|Ama no Uzume|de|Amenouzume|el|Άμε Νο Ουζούμε|eo|Ame no Uzume|es|Ame-no-Uzume|fa|آمه نو اوزومه|fr|Uzume|hr|Ame-no-Uzume|hu|Ame-no-Uzume|id|Ama-no-Uzume|it|Ama-no-Uzume|ja|アメノウズメ|jv|Ama-no-Uzume|ka|ამე-ნო უძუმე|ko|아메노우즈메|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯎꯓꯨꯃꯦ|no|Ama-no-Uzume|pl|Amenouzume|pt|Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto|ru|Амэ-но удзумэ|simple|Ame-no-Uzume|sv|Uzume|th|อาเมะ โนะ อูซูเมะ|tr|Ame-no-Uzume|uk|Ама-но-Удзуме-но-Мікото|zh|天鈿女命|qid=Q462803|lt=Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto}} and {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|az|Sarutahiko|fa|ساروتاهیکو اوکامی|fr|Sarutahiko Ōkami|it|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|サルタヒコ|ko|사루타히코 오카미|mni|ꯁꯔꯨꯇꯍꯤꯀꯣ ꯑꯣꯀꯃꯤ|pl|Sarutahiko|ru|Сарутахико|simple|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ta|சருதாகிகோ அகாமி|tr|Sarutahiko Ōkami|zh|猿田彥|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto}} as secondary deities (associated deities).

Hieda no Are is regarded as a deity of learning and storytelling. Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto is the progenitor deity of the performing arts. Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto is a deity of land and directions, and the husband deity of Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto. Hieda no Are came from the Hieda clan of the {{ill|Sarume clan|fr|Clan Sarumé|ja|猿女君|simple|Sarume clan|qid=Q11572091}}, and Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto is the {{ill|Oyagami|Q85882782|qid=Q85882782}} and {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} of the Sarume no Kimi.

In the Middle Ages, the enshrined deity was described as “unknown.”

=== History ===
Hieda was the home base of the Hieda clan of the Sarume no Kimi, who traced their ancestry to Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto, and it is thought that the shrine was founded by the time of the Asuka period under Empress Suiko as an ancestral mausoleum-shrine. In the {{ill|Nara period|Q189178|qid=Q189178}}, along the western edge of the Hieda settlement ran the “Shimotsu-michi,” a major arterial route usable by both land and water that connected to {{ill|Heijō-kyō|Q862509|qid=Q862509}}. Because many ritual implements were excavated from there, it is believed that this shrine once stood near the {{ill|Rajōmon|Q1344338|qid=Q1344338}} of {{ill|Heijō-kyō|Q862509|qid=Q862509}}, where it served to purify the defilement of people entering and leaving the capital and to pray for traffic safety, thus also functioning as a {{ill|Dōsojin|Q269515|qid=Q269515}} (roadside guardian deity).

It is recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} as “{{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}}{{ill|Soekami District, Nara|ja|添上郡|ko|소에카미군|pt|Distrito de Soekami (Nara)|zh|添上郡|qid=Q7553491}} Meta Shrine,” and is listed as a minor shrine.

As for the origin of the shrine’s name, a widely accepted theory holds that the Sarume no Kimi were granted many cultivated fields by the emperor, which were called Sarume fields, and their owners were called Sarumeta-nushi. Later, the character for “saru” (monkey) was abbreviated, and they came to be called Onna-ta-nushi, and the shrine that enshrined their ancestral deity came to be called “Meta Shrine.”

Until the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was called “Sansha Myōjin.” In {{ill|1874|Q7761|qid=Q7761}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 7) it became “Jūsansha Myōjin,” in {{ill|1891|Q7837|qid=Q7837}} (Meiji 24) it was renamed “Urita Shrine,” and in {{ill|1942|Q18625|qid=Q18625}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 17) it was renamed to its current name, “Meta Shrine.”

=== Festivals ===
=== Are Festival ===
The Are Festival (Areisai) is a festival commemorating the virtues of Hieda no Are. It was begun in {{ill|1930|Q18787|qid=Q18787}} (Shōwa 5) by children’s literature author {{ill|Kurushima Takehiko|Q6447506|qid=Q6447506}}, who, with the cooperation of folktale writers from across the country, proposed that Hieda no Are was most fitting as a “god of stories” comparable to {{ill|Hans Christian Andersen|Q5673|qid=Q5673|lt=Andersen}}.

After the offering of the Hieda dance, local children dedicate the Are-sama Ondo and the Are-sama Festival Children’s Song. Storytelling and read-aloud sessions of fairy tales are also held.

On April 30, {{ill|2012|Q1990|qid=Q1990}} (Heisei 24), a celebratory festival honoring Hieda no Are was held to commemorate the 1,300th anniversary of the compilation of the {{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}{{ill|compilation|Q11607994|qid=Q11607994}}.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120430230832/http://sankei.jp.msn.com/life/news/120430/art12043016350003-n1.htm Celebratory festival honoring Hieda no Are for the 1,300th anniversary of the Kojiki compilation] Sankei Shimbun, accessed April 30, 2012</ref>.

It had long been held every year on {{ill|August 16|Q2812|qid=Q2812}}, but in consideration of recent {{ill|Summer|Q1313|qid=Q1313}} {{ill|extreme heat|Q3774617|qid=Q3774617}}, it was decided that starting in {{ill|2025|Q49616|qid=Q49616}} ({{ill|Reiwa era|Q62609017|qid=Q62609017}} 7) it would be changed to {{ill|May 5|ab|Лаҵарамза 5|af|5 Mei|als|5.
